about: Measured walk timings by number of lanes (independent chains), drawn by the 'Why 32 couriers beat one' page (assets/javascripts/couriers.js), one chart a panel, each on its own axes. Only measured points go here, each panel naming its source. Panels are never compared with each other: they differ in machine, corpus, clock and implementation. To add a sweep, append a panel; nothing else changes.

panels.title: K chains through one block, unjoined
panels.what: The prototype's latency test (bz2k walkm): K independent chains walked in lockstep through one freshly built T-vector, with no segment bookkeeping and no join. A ceiling for the joined walk, not a decoder.
panels.measured: Local, one thread: an Intel Xeon VM at 2.1 GHz (TSC cycles), the wikidata-pq bench slice's blocks.

panels.title: The flagged walk by lane count, with and without the prefetch
panels.what: walk_segments_flagged_with::<LANES, PREFETCH> at 512 segments: the joined walk as the decoder runs it, before the shared-offset walk (#37). PR #21 also gives 256 and 1,024 segments.
panels.measured: Local, one thread, pinned: the walk alone on half of the 431 Wikidata dump blocks in CI's corpus, best of 3, cycles at a nominal 2.8 GHz on a shared VM. Exploratory: it picked candidates, CI's bench decided.
